findings.claim: RuntimeConfigStore and the frontend parser preserve the value, but production constructs one WsRouter without realtime options, upgrades only /ws, and the browser creates one hard-coded /ws socket.
The value is stored per session and printed in the overflow error, but both observe and bounded modes use the same bounded queue and degrade behavior.

Definite allocations occur at server JSON.stringify/Buffer.byteLength, browser JSON.parse, TextEncoder byte counting, coalescing joins, UTF-8 prefix slices, and recovery/grace string concatenation. Whether JavaScript engines materialize every intermediate string immediately is unmeasured.

The 300ms remount grace buffer concatenates output without a configured cap and flushes session:ready before the buffered snapshot. This can release the input gate before snapshot application and changes original wire ordering.

Hidden recovery clears skipped/dirty state immediately after a local snapshot restore, before the requested authoritative server repair succeeds. A later repair rejection only clears visible-recovery state, so a stale local snapshot can remain without hidden recovery being retried.

Snapshot replacement, local restore, repair patch, and recovery tail do not share the bounded visible scheduler. FR-BGSTAB-017 explicitly records this as planned work and requires ACK/input release after recovery drain.

Screen-repair pending overflow aborts the barrier by concatenating/flushing all queued plus current output rather than converting pressure to bounded snapshot refresh. Existing server tests lock in this current behavior, while REL-BGSTAB-003 remains planned.
Output received while TerminalView is absent or restorePending is pushed into bufferedOutputRef without byte or chunk limits; later restore joins all chunks.

safe-send serializes each message with JSON.stringify, classifies it into control or one global terminal lane per socket, optionally coalesces adjacent same-session output, and performs one callback-serialized ws.send at a time.
The frontend runtime parser retains the value, but TerminalView constructs xterm with literal scrollback: 10000. Server headless scrollback uses the distinct pty.scrollbackLines field.
BuilderGate has no @xterm/addon-webgl dependency and its active terminal path is the DOM renderer.

Ctrl+C selection copy clears the selection immediately without awaiting or handling navigator.clipboard.writeText, while context-menu paste bypasses TerminalView.pasteInput and calls sendInput directly.

Current requirements cover queue bounds, recovery, split transport, hidden output and registered preset paste, but do not explicitly cover per-session output fairness, bounded remount grace buffering, renderer authority, WebGL lifecycle, or ordinary selection/copy/paste ownership.
